Nergal: Nergal ({d}NER.URU.GAL, the star + NER + URU + GAL; Harper’s sign list no. 170) — the strong god of battle: Nergal dannum ina ilī “Nergal, the strong one among the gods”
Ninkarrak: Ninkarrak ({d}NIN.KAR.RA.AK, the star + NIN + KAR + RA + AK) — the physician-goddess, mārat Anim “daughter of Anum”
aggum: angry, enraged (the adjective is my reading, UNCERTAIN; Harper’s glossary has aggu “anger”): aggim (ag-gi-im, genitive, AK read ag) in ina libbiša aggim “in her angry heart”
apum: reed-bed, thicket, canebrake (Harper’s abu “cane, reeds”): apim (a-bi-im, BI read pi₂ or bi, genitive) in ša apim “of the reed thicket”; the form could also be abim “of the father”, which does not fit
ašakkum: ašakku — the name of a sickness (Harper’s asakku “disease”), written with two signs, Á and a second sign not identified (shown ?): ašakkam (Á.?, accusative) “an ašakku”; the second sign and the exact sense are UNCERTAIN
binûtum: Harper’s binûtu “muscle, life”; here “body” (my choice, UNCERTAIN): biniātišu (bi-ni-a-ti-šu, plural biniātu + -šu) “his body”
damum: blood: dāmīšunu (da-mi-šu-nu, plural dāmū, here accusative dāmī, + -šunu) “their blood”
damāmum: to lament, mourn (Harper’s damāmu I,2, a t-stem): liddammam (li-id-dam-ma-am, precative with the ventive -am) “let him mourn”; the exact form is UNCERTAIN
dumqum: kindness, favour (Harper’s dumqu): dumqīya (dum-qi₂-ia, KI read qi₂) “my kindness”; qābiat dumqīya “who speaks of my kindness”, UNCERTAIN as an idiom
gurunnum: heap, pile (Harper’s gurunnu): gurun (gu-ru-un, the form before a genitive) “a heap of”: gurun šalmat “a heap of corpses”
idlūtum: manhood, vigour (Harper’s edlūtu “manhood, vigor”, ed-lu-ti-šu): idlūtišu (id-lu-ti-šu, the A₂ sign read id) “his manhood”, UNCERTAIN
imittum: right side, right hand: imnīya (im-ni-ia, imittum + -ia) “my right”: ālik imnīya “who goes at my right”
izuzzum-Š: Š-stem of izuzzum “to stand”: to make stand, set up · lišziz (li-iš-zi-iz, Š precative) “let him set up”: nakiršu elīšu lišziz “let him set his enemy up against him”
išītum: confusion (Harper’s išîtu “confusion, revolt”): išītam (i-ši-tam, accusative) “confusion”, UNCERTAIN
kamûm: to bind (the verb behind Harper’s KAMÎŠ “bound”): kamiš (ka-mi-iš, adverb in -iš; Harper has KAMÎŠ “bound” as its own entry) “bound, in bonds”, UNCERTAIN
kašūšum: Harper’s kašûšu “power, strength”: kašūšišu (ka-šu-ši-šu, kašūšum + -šu, genitive) “his kašūšu, his might”; the sense is UNCERTAIN (a name for a divine weapon is also possible)
kirbītum: midst (Harper’s kirbitu): kirbit (kir-bi-it, the form before a genitive) “the midst of”: ina kirbit nišīšu “in the midst of his people”; UNCERTAIN as a word
malûm-D: D-stem of malûm “to be full”: to fill; with ana qāt, to hand over to · limallišuma (li-ma-al-li-šu-ma, D precative + -šu “him” + -ma “and”) “let her hand him over, and”: ana qāt nakrišu limallišuma “into the hand of his enemy let her deliver him, and”
maqātum-Š: Š-stem of maqātum “to fall”: to make fall, fell · lišamqit (li-ša-am-qi₂-it, Š precative, KI read qi₂; Harper prints ki) “let her make fall”
murṣum: illness, sickness (Harper’s murṣu): murṣam (mur-ṣa-am, accusative, HAR read mur) “an illness”: murṣam kabtam “a heavy illness”
mūšum: night: mūšim (mu-ši-im, genitive) in ana mūšim “into night”
naḫûm-D: D-stem of naḫûm “to be quiet” (Harper’s naḫû II,1 “to pacify, to allay”): to quiet, give ease to · unaḫḫuššu (u-na-aḫ-ḫu-šu, unaḫḫuš, D present, + -šu “him”, the two š written once) “he gives him ease”: lā unaḫḫuššu “he does not give him ease”
nišqum: bite (Harper’s nišqu): nišiq (ni-ši-iq, construct, IG read iq) “the bite of”: nišiq mūtim “the bite of death”; not našāqum “to kiss”; the exact sense is UNCERTAIN
pašāḫum: to become calm, to calm (Harper’s pašāḫu I,1 “to be healed, to be cured”): ipaššeḫu (i-pa-aš-še-ḫu, present with the -u of a ša-clause) “(which the physician) calms”, UNCERTAIN whether transitive or intransitive
qamûm: to burn (Harper’s kamû I,1 “to burn”, li-ik-me; the form is UNCERTAIN): liqme (li-iq-me, IG read iq, precative) “let him burn”
saḫmaštum: revolt, rebellion (Harper’s saḫmaštu, filed under S): saḫmaštam (za-aḫ-ma-aš-tam, ZA read sa, accusative) “revolt”, UNCERTAIN
tamḫārum: battle (UD read tam): tamḫārim (tam-ḫa-ri-im, genitive) “of battle”: ašar tamḫārim “in the place of battle”
taḫāzum: battle, conflict (Harper’s taḫāzu): taḫāzim “of battle”, written with the single sign AK (Harper’s sign list no. 48); which Sumerogram it is I do not know, so the reading from his normalization and the sense are UNCERTAIN; the key AK is the sign’s shape only
uzzatum: wrath, anger: uzzatiša (uz-za-ti-ša, uzzatum + -ša, genitive; the adjective with it is plural, so the noun is read as a plural of intensity) “her wrath”: ina uzzatiša rabêtim “in her great wrath”
šalmatum: corpse (feminine of šalmum): šalmat (ša-al-ma-at, the form before a genitive) “corpse of”, in gurun šalmat ummānātišu “a heap of the corpses of his troops”
šētum: wall (?) (Harper’s šētu, with his query): šēt (še-it, construct) in šēt bītim “the wall (?) of the house”, UNCERTAIN
ḫapāšum: to break, crush, shatter (Harper’s ḫapāšu I,1): liḫpuš (li-iḫ-pu-uš, G precative) “let him smash”
ṣimdum: bandage (Harper’s simdu, written zi-im-di with ZI read ṣi): ṣimdi (ṣi-im-di, genitive) “by a bandage”, in ina ṣimdi; not ṣimdatum “ordinance”
ṭīṭum: clay (the plate has two DI signs, read ṭi-ṭi; Harper prints di-di-im): ṭīṭim (ṭi-ṭi-im, genitive) “of clay”: ṣalam ṭīṭim “an image of clay”

__broaden__.balûm: to go out (of fire); D-stem bullûm “to extinguish”: ana bullîm “to put (it) out” · to destroy, bring to an end (Harper’s balû I,1): ibêllû (i-bi-el-lu-u, present 3rd plural with the -u of a clause) “they destroy”; the exact verb is UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.rêʾûm-pasture: to pasture, graze (a herd): the infinitive in the genitive after ana, ana … rēʾîm “to pasture” (ri-im), said rēʾîm; the spelling ri-im is Harper’s and the reading of the word as the infinitive of rêʾûm (the verb behind rēʾûm “shepherd”) is my own from the grammar, UNCERTAIN · lirʾi (li-ri, precative) “let him shepherd”: nišīšu ina mīšarim lirʾi “let him shepherd his people in justice”; the spelling li-ri has no sign for the ʾ, and Harper files it under another verb (ARU II,1 “to carry, to rule”), so the reading is UNCERTAIN · lirʾûšu (li-ru-šu, 3rd plural precative + -šu “him”, the ʾ not written) “let them herd him”, of a captive led away, UNCERTAIN (Harper files li-ru-šu under aru II,1 “to carry, to rule”)
__broaden__.kakkum: weapon: kakkim (GIŠ.TUKUL, Sumerogram, no ending written; genitive after ina) “of the weapon”; Harper’s glossary gives no spelling, and the second sign (keyed TUK) is TENTATIVE · kakkašu, kakkišu (GIŠ.TUKUL-šu, Sumerogram + -šu) “his weapon”; kakkīya (GIŠ.TUKUL-ia) “my weapons”
__broaden__.arārum: to curse (Harper’s araru I,1): lirur (li-ru-ur, precative) “let him curse” · lirurū (li-ru-ru, precative with the plural -ū) “let them curse” · liruršuma (li-ru-ur-šu-ma, precative + -šu “him” + -ma “and”) “let him curse him, and”
__broaden__.dannum: the strong one: ina dīnim ana dannim ištarak “in a lawsuit he handed (him) to the strong” · strong, mighty (adjective): dannim (genitive) “strong”, danniātim (da-ni-a-tim, feminine plural genitive) “mighty”
__broaden__.ṣalmum: statue, image (Harper’s salmu): ṣalmīya (ALAN-ia) “my statue”; the sign ALAN is TENTATIVE, the word being unspelled in Harper’s glossary · ṣalam (ṣa-lam, the form before a genitive) “image of”: ṣalam ṭīṭim “an image of clay”
__broaden__.ummānum: army, host: ummānišu (um-ma-ni-šu) “his army”; išid ummānišu “the foundation of his army” · ummānšu (um-ma-an-šu) “his troops”; ummānātišu (um-ma-na-ti-šu, plural ummānāt + -šu) “his troops”
__broaden__.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law · alākišu (a-la-ki-šu) “his going” (infinitive with -šu): ina alākišu “in his going” · Gt present ittallak (it-ta-al-la-ak) “she shall go away” (the Gt gives the sense of going off; the Gtn would be ittanallak) · ittalak “she has gone” (perfect): ana šīmtim ittalak “she has gone to her fate” · ittalku (it-ta-al-ku) with the subjunctive -u: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate” · ittalkamma (it-ta-al-kam-ma) perfect ittalkam (ittalak + the ventive -am, “hither”) “he has come”, + -ma “and” · lillikma (li-il-li-ik-ma, li- + illik + -ma) “let him go, and” · illakā (i-la-ka) “they go”, present 3rd feminine plural, agreeing with a feminine plural noun: ša šīmātūšu ina maḫra illakā “whose fates go in front” · ālik (a-li-ku, participle with the -u kept before a genitive) “who goes”: ālik imnīya “who goes at my right”
__broaden__.nadûm: to cast, throw (a charge; a body into the river): iddi, nadû, iddû · also to leave lying (a field): ittadi “he has left (it) lying” · of a flock: ṣēnī ana eqlim iddi “he turned the sheep loose into a field” · inaddûši (i-na-[ad]-du-u-ši) “they shall throw her” (present, plural, with -ši): ana mê inaddûši “they shall throw her into the water” · inaddûši “they shall throw him” of a man (§155, ana mê inaddûši), UNCERTAIN because the suffix -ši is “her” elsewhere · of a tooth, to knock out: ittadi (it-ta-di, perfect) “he has knocked out”, inaddû (i-na-ad-du-u, present plural) “they shall knock out”: šinni awīlim ittadi “he has knocked out a man’s tooth” · addi (ad-di, preterite, 1st person) “I let drop”: aḫī ul addi “I did not let my arm drop”, the idiom of aḫšu iddi · littaddi (li-it-ta-ad-di, precative with infixed -t-, Harper’s nadû I,2; the stem is UNCERTAIN) “let her cast down”
__broaden__.damqum: good, gracious; damiqtim “gracious” · damqātišu (dam-qa₂-ti-šu, feminine plural damqātum + -šu) “his good things” · damiqtum (da-mi-iq-tum, feminine nominative, IG read iq) “gracious”: lamassī damiqtum “my gracious guardian spirit”
__broaden__.qatûm-Š: Š-stem of qatûm “to come to an end” (Harper’s qatû III,1): to bring to an end, cut off · lišaqti (li-ša-aq-ti, Š precative; AK read aq) “let him bring to an end” · lišaqtišuma (li-ša-ti-šu-ma, precative + -šu “him” + -ma “and”) “let him bring him to an end, and”: the spelling has no aq (Harper’s glossary has li-ša-[ak]-ti-šu, the aq bracketed), so the form is UNCERTAIN: ina kakkišu dannim lišaqtišuma “with his strong weapon let him bring him to an end (?), and”
__broaden__.kašādum: to reach, overcome: iktašassu “(the River) has overcome him” · likšussu (li-ik-šu-zu, precative + -šu, the d and š said ss, written ZU) “let it reach him, overtake him” · likšudaššu (li-ik-šu-da-šu, precative + the ventive -am + -šu “him”, the m said š) “let it overtake him”: arḫiš likšudaššu “let it overtake him quickly”
__broaden__.kašādum-Š: Š-stem of kašādum: to cause to reach: uštakšidaššu “he got him back (to his city)” · mušakšidu (mu-ša-ak-ši-du, participle, the -u kept) “who brings about, who gives”: mušakšidu irnittīya “who brings about my victory”
__broaden__.petûm: to open; of land, to bring into cultivation: iptete “he has opened” · preterite ipte, iptēma “he opened” · iptēma (ip-te-ma) “he has opened, and”, of a part of the body, with a knife · pātiat (pa-ti-a-at, feminine participle, the form before a genitive) “who opens”: pātiat kakkīya “who opens my weapons”, UNCERTAIN as a picture
__broaden__.râmum: to love: irammu (i-ra-am-mu, present), with the subjunctive -u after ša: ša irammu “whom he/she loves” · rāʾimat (ra-i-ma-at, feminine participle, the form before a genitive) “who loves”: rāʾimat palêya “who loves my reign”
__broaden__.banûm: to build, create; ibniušu “whom he created” · bānītī (ba-ni-ti, feminine participle + -ī “my”; Harper’s banîtu “mother”) “my creator”: ummum bānītī “the mother, my creator” · ibni (ib-ni, preterite, after ay) “he creates, begets”: ay ibni “may he not beget”
__broaden__.târum-D: D-stem of târum: to give back: turru “taken away/captured”; utarrūšumma “they shall return (it) to him” · utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · turrim (infinitive, tu-ur-ri-im): ana turrim “for repaying, to give back”; utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · uttēr (ut-te-ir, perfect) “he has given back”: the same verb as utâr · litēršu (li-te-ir-šu, precative + -šu, Harper’s taru II,1) “let him turn back / take back from him”, UNCERTAIN: melam šarrūtim litēršu “let him turn the glory of kingship away from him” · litēr (li-te-ir, precative, without a suffix) “let him turn”: ana tīl abūbim litēr “let him turn (it) into a mound of the flood” · litēršum (li-te-ir-šum, precative + -šum “for him”) and litēršumma (li-te-ir-šum-ma, + -ma “and”) “let him turn (it) for him”: ūmam ana mūšim litēršumma “let him turn the day into night for him” · litēršuma (li-te-ir-šu-ma, precative + -šu “from him” + -ma “and”) “let her turn (a son) away from him, and”, UNCERTAIN as litēršu above
__broaden__.lamassum: the lamassu — protective guardian spirit (the KAL sign) · lamassī (la-ma-zi, “my lamassu”, the zi written for -ssī): lamassī damiqtum “my gracious guardian spirit”
__broaden__.waṣûm-Š: Š-stem of waṣûm “to go out”: to send out, bring out; of land, to take on lease: ana irrišūtim ušēṣi “he took (a field) for cultivation” · ušeṣṣûšu (u-še-iz-zu-u-šu) “they shall make him go out” (present plural + -šu “him”; Harper writes ṣ as z): ālam ušeṣṣûšu “they shall drive him out of the city” · šuṣâ (šu-ṣa-a; Harper’s su-sa-a, under III,1) “brought out (?)”: the form (a stative plural? an imperative?) and its subject are UNCERTAIN · lišaṣiaššumma (li-ša-ṣi-a-aš-šum-ma, Š precative + the ventive -am + -šum “for him” + -ma “and”) “let her bring out for him, and”: ina biniātišu lišaṣiaššumma “let her make (them) break out on him in his body, and”
__broaden__.šaqûm: to give to drink; Š-stem — mušešqi “who waters” · lišqi (li-iš-qi₂, G precative, KI read qi₂) “let her give to drink”: erṣetam lišqi “let her make the earth drink”
__broaden__.rašûm-Š: to cause to acquire (Š-stem of rašûm “to acquire, get”; double accusative): ušaršušu (u-šar-šu-šu) “who has made him acquire (children)” (ušarši + the subjunctive -u + -šu “him”); the analysis of the ending is UNCERTAIN · ušaršišināti (u-šar-ši-ši-na-ti, 1st person) “I let them get”: mugallitam ul ušaršišināti “I let no molester have them” · ušarši (u-šar-ši, preterite, after ay) “she lets (him) obtain”, ušaršīšu (u-šar-ši-šu, + -šu “him”): ay ušarši šuāti “may she not let him obtain”; šumam ay ušaršīšu “may she not let him obtain a name”
__broaden__.nasāḫum-N: N-stem of nasāḫum, the passive: to be uprooted, cast out (of a family house): innassaḫ (in-na-az-za-aḫ) “he shall be cast out” · innassaḫu (in-na-za-ḫu, present with the -u of the clause, za for -ssa- as in innassaḫ) “is removed”: lā innassaḫu “which is not removed”
__broaden__.lamādum: to learn, to know; of a person, to know carnally (Harper): iltamad (il-ta-ma-ad, perfect) “he has known (his daughter)”; ilmassi (il-ma-zi) “he has known her” (preterite ilmad + -ši “her”, d + š said ss, spelled with the sign ZI); ilmassima (il-ma-zi-ma) “has known her, and” · ilammadu (i-lam-ma-du, present with the -u of the clause) “he knows”: kirībšu lā ilammadu “he does not know its inside”
__broaden__.ašrum: place; ana ašrišu “to its (proper) place” · ašar “where”, with a verb in the subjunctive: ašar illiku “where he went” · ašar (a-šar, the form before a genitive) “the place of”: ašar tamḫārim “in the place of battle”
__broaden__.qablum: battle, combat · qablê (MURUB₄.MURUB₄, the sign doubled, plural genitive) “of combats”: taḫāzim u qablê “of battle and of combats” · qabal (qa₂-ba-al, the form before a genitive) “the battle of”: qabal lā maḫār “battle none can face”
__broaden__.ṣīrum: lofty, exalted · ṣīrtum (ṣi-ir-tum, feminine nominative) “exalted”: bēltum ṣīrtum “the exalted lady”
__broaden__.ezzum: furious, raging (Harper’s ezzu, adverb ezziš “furiously”) · izziš (iz-zi-iš, with i for e, adverb in -iš) “furiously” · izzitim (iz-zi-tim, feminine genitive; Harper’s ez-zi-tim) “fierce”: išātim izzitim “of fierce fire”
__broaden__.Anum: Anum — the sky-god · Anim (AN.NIM, the signs AN and NIM, genitive) “of Anum”: mārat Anim “daughter of Anum”
__broaden__.mūtum: death (mūtum; not mutum “husband”): mūt (mu-ut, the form before a genitive) “death of” · mūtim (mu-tim, genitive) “of death”: nišiq mūtim “the bite of death”
__broaden__.lemnum: evil, bad: lemnam (lim-nam, accusative) “an evil omen” · lemnētim (li-im-ne-tim, feminine plural genitive) “evil things”: ana lemnētim “into evil”
__broaden__.rabûm: great; D/Š-stems “make great”; rabûtim “great (pl.)” · rabîtim (ra-bi-tim, feminine genitive) “large”: ina abnim rabîtim “by the large stone” · rabītišu (ra-bi-ti-šu) “his senior one”, the feminine with -šu: read as the father’s chief wife, UNCERTAIN · rabîm (ra-bi-im, genitive) “great”: ina kašūšišu rabîm “by his great kašūšu” · rabêtim (ra-be-a-tim, feminine plural genitive) “great”: ina uzzatiša rabêtim “in her great wrath” · rabûti (GAL.GAL, plural) “great”: ilāni rabûti “the great gods”
__broaden__.mātum: land, country · māt (ma-at) the form before a following genitive, “the land of”: ina māt nukurtim “in a hostile country” · mātim (ma-tim, or the Sumerogram KALAM, no ending written) genitive “of the land”: ina libbu mātim “in the middle of the land”, mārū mātim “natives of the country”, mātim šanītim “another country” · mātassu (ma-zu, with -šu “his”, the t and š said ss and written with ZU) “his land”; mātišu (ma-ti-šu) “his land” · mātātim (ma-ta-tim, plural genitive) “of the lands”: bēltum ṣīrtum ša mātātim “the exalted lady of the lands”
__broaden__.irritum: curse (Harper’s irritu): irrītīya (ir-ri-ti-ia) “my curses” (with -ia “my”) · irrīt (ir-ri-it, the form before a genitive) “the curse of” · irrītim (ir-ri-tim, genitive) “of the curse”: aššum irrītim šināti “because of those curses” · irritam (ir-ri-tam, accusative) “a curse”, the cognate object of arārum: irritam marūštam lirurū “let them curse with a grievous curse” · irrītim (ir-ri-tim, genitive, here taken as a plural) “curses”: irrītim danniātim “with mighty curses”
